steps: Plan before framing
Settle heat transfer kits (up to (2)), Kozy Power Vent (#KPV, horizontal only) and any propane conversion first; doing either conversion after installation means removing the control board.
Stand-offs & nailing flanges

Form and attach the top stand-offs (5-5/16" to header) before setting the unit; remove, form and reattach the back stand-offs. Nailing flanges give 1-1/8" to side framing and are never permanently removed.
Rough framing
Min. opening 47" H × 48-3/4" W × 27-1/4" D, 80" from base to enclosure top. Level, on wood or a non-combustible surface (not linoleum or carpet); insulate outside walls.
Vent pass-through framing
Keep 1" around vertical pipe, 3" above and 1" beside/below horizontal pipe. Use an #800-WPT series thimble through walls; never recess the vent cap.

Clearances from the vent pipe to combustibles:

Vertical vent pipe1" (25mm) on all sides
Horizontal pipe, top3" (76mm)
Horizontal pipe, sides and bottom1" (25mm)

Wall pass-throughs

4½" (114mm) to 6½" (165mm) wall#800-WPT
6½" (165mm) to 12½" (318mm) wall#800-WPT2
4" (101mm) to 6½" (165mm) wall#800-WPT3

A #800-WPT series thimble, or one that keeps the required 3" (76mm) top clearance, is required wherever a horizontal run passes through an interior or exterior wall. ICC wall pass-through TM-5WT is also approved. Metal Fab vent needs an adapter, which raises the minimum height to the center of the vent pipe by 3-1/4" (83mm) when framing the pass-through.

Horizontal sections need 1/4" (6mm) rise for every 12" (305mm) of travel for natural draft. Do not recess the vent cap into the wall or siding. The minimum horizontal termination framing dimensions are shown as a diagram on p. 17.
Facing, mantel & safety barrier

Non-combustible facing up to 1/2" thick at top and sides, only to the finishing edge so the glass frame stays removable; no screws in the lower left corner. Mantel per the clearance rules; the barrier hangs on (4) top and (4) hearth-plate magnets.
Gas line connection
Qualified installer (licensed plumber or gas fitter in Massachusetts). Connect the 1/2" tee-handle shut-off and flex connector to the 1/2" valve inlet through a side access hole, clear of the fan.
Vent system & termination

Approved 5" × 8" co-axial system within the run limits; restrictor plate as needed; horizontal heat shield on minimum horizontal runs; terminate per the clearance table. Never share a solid-fuel flue.

• Restrictor plate (components packet): ships with its (2) inner rings intact for the most restriction. Remove the innermost ring for less restriction, all inner rings for the least. Bend the tabs to approx. 80° and slide it into the exhaust pipe, tabs toward you, before attaching venting (or later through the baffle).
  • Horizontal vent heat shield: required on minimum horizontal venting. Loosen the (2) screws in front of the flue collar, bend the shield to 90° at the perforation, slide its (2) slots under the screws and re-tighten.
  • #800-1 flex kits: don't attach the #844-1 or #845-1 kit to the fireplace until it has passed through the wall. Minimum bend radius to center 6 in (152 mm). Each #846-1 extension adds 6' (1.83 m); don't stretch beyond what is required. Use the included vinyl siding protector on vinyl siding.
  • Provide a means for visually checking the vent connection after the fireplace is installed.

Termination clearances (selected)

A · above grade, veranda, porch, deck, balcony12" (30cm)
B · window or door that may be openedUS 9" (23cm) · Canada 12" (30cm)
J · non-mechanical air supply inletUS 9" (23cm) · Canada 12" (30cm)
K · mechanical air supply inletUS 3' (91cm) above if within 10' (3m) horizontally (Massachusetts: 10' (3m)) · Canada 6' (1.83m)
N / O · between two terminations12" (30cm)

The full A–P table and its drawing are on p. 29. Clearances are to heat-resistant material, not vinyl; Hussong Mfg. is not responsible for heat damage from terminating under vinyl overhangs, ceilings or soffits. Vertical caps: minimum height from roof to lowest discharge opening runs from 1.0 ft (flat to 6/12) to 8.0 ft (over 20/12 to 21/12); see the roof-pitch table on p. 28.
Liner kit & log set

A firebox liner kit is required (risk of fire without it). If converting to propane, do it first. Place logs #1 to #11 per the figures, off the burner ports; lava rock on the floor refractory, rockwool embers brushed on.
Power & control setup
Grounded, always-hot, unswitched supply. Batteries in, packaging out, then sync: sync button (3 beeps), remote ON/OFF within 5 seconds (4 beeps); rocker switch to ON.

1. Set the main ON/OFF rocker switch to OFF. Install (4) AA batteries (not included) in the backup battery holder on the control module and (3) AAA batteries (included) in the remote.
  2. Connect the IFC module to AC power.
  3. Remove all packaging and combustible material from the firebox. The next steps start the pilot in manual mode: the igniter sparks repeatedly and the pilot lights if gas is supplied.
  4. Remove the hearth plate and component access doors to reach the toggle switch and remote sync button on the left side.
  5. Press the remote sync button: (3) beeps and an amber LED.
  6. Within (5) seconds press ON/OFF on the remote: (4) beeps, and the pilot lights.
  7. Press ON/OFF again: the pilot goes out and the system is initialized.
  8. Set the rocker switch to ON for remote operation.

Manual operation (no remote): rocker switch OFF, press the sync button until (3) beeps and the amber LED, then press it again within (5) seconds. The pilot lights; the rocker switch then runs the main burner on HI only.
Pressure test & flame check
Check inlet pressure with all other gas appliances running, then manifold pressure. Burn 15 minutes and tune the venturi or restrictor plate per Tables 11.4 and 11.5.

Inlet pressure at tap IN (A) with all other gas appliances on; manifold pressure at tap OUT (B). Use a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose, retighten each tap snug, and confirm with the manometer that it reads no pressure.

Let the fireplace cool before any adjustment, and burn it at least 15 minutes before judging the flame. Flames start blue and should turn yellow over the first 15 minutes. If there is soot on the glass, check log placement before adjusting the venturi. Venturi adjustment must be done by a qualified service technician; keep both inlet tubes at the same opening.

Venturi (Table 11.4)

Dark, orange flame with black tipsclosed too far: open slightly
Short, blue flamesopen too far: close slightly
Lifting (ghosting) flamesgas pressure too high (check manometer) or venturi closed too far (open slightly)

Restrictor plate (Table 11.5)

Short, flickeringexcessive draft: add restrictor
Lifting or ghostinginsufficient draft: remove inner ring(s) or the restrictor

If flames still lift or ghost after opening the restrictor and verifying the vent installation, shut off the gas supply and call a qualified service technician. Vertical terminations may show an active, compact flame.

Note: on the venturi direction for blue, lifting flames, p. 52 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and its Table 11.4 says to close the venturi slightly for short, blue flames but to open it slightly for lifting (ghosting) flames; the manual's troubleshooting chart on p. 55 says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner.

light.title: Lighting the fireplace
light.html:
Your fireplace lights itself. An electronic igniter sparks the pilot, and the pilot lights the burner. Never try to light the pilot by hand.

Everyday use

  1. Press the ON/OFF key on the remote. The fireplace answers with a single beep.
  2. About 4 seconds later the igniter starts sparking at the pilot. Once the pilot is lit, the burner comes on.
  3. Press ON/OFF again to turn the burner off.

For the remote to run the burner, the main ON/OFF rocker switch must be on. It sits on the left side, behind the hearth plate and component access doors.

Full lighting instructions

  1. Read the safety information first.
  2. Press OFF on the remote, then turn off all electric power to the fireplace.
  3. Turn the manual gas valve clockwise to OFF. Use only your hand, never tools. If the valve won't turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified service technician. Force or attempted repair may cause a fire or explosion.
  4. Wait 5 minutes, then smell for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop and see "Safety & gas smell."
  5. Turn the manual valve counterclockwise to ON.
  6. Turn the electric power back on and press ON on the remote.
Still won't run? Turn off the gas: press OFF on the remote, turn off all electric power to the fireplace if it is going to be serviced, then find the manual valve your service technician installed and turn it clockwise to OFF. Call your service technician or gas supplier.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The Proflame 2 remote runs on (3) AAA batteries, which come with the fireplace.

  • ON/OFF key: turns the fireplace on (a single beep, then it starts lighting) and off.
  • Flame: 6 levels. The down arrow lowers the flame one level at a time, down to off. The up arrow raises it one step. If the flame is off while the system is on, the up arrow relights it on HI.
  • Thermostat key: press once for room thermostat, then set the temperature with the arrows. Press until "SMART" appears and the remote turns the flame down as the room reaches your set temperature. While smart thermostat is on, you can't adjust the flame by hand.
  • Mode key: steps to the fan (6 speeds) and the accent light (6 levels). Adjust with the arrows.
  • Key lock: press Mode and the up arrow together. A lock icon appears.
  • °F or °C: with the system off, press Thermostat and Mode together.
Fan timing: in thermostat mode the fan waits 5 minutes after the fire lights and keeps running about 12 minutes after it turns off. In manual mode it runs at its last setting with no delay.

A battery icon on the remote's screen means its batteries are low. It disappears once you replace them.

sounds.title: First fire: what's normal
sounds.html:
A few things you notice in the first fires are normal.

Foggy glass

When you first light the fireplace, condensation appears on the glass. This happens in all gas fireplaces and clears after several minutes.

A paint smell

Expect a paint smell during the first few hours of burning. Leave the fan off during this time. It helps the paint cure faster.

Ticks and creaks

The metal expands as it heats and contracts as it cools, so you may hear noises. This is normal and doesn't affect how well or how long the fireplace works.

Blue flames at first

When the fireplace is first lit, the flames look blue. Over the first 15 minutes they gradually turn the yellow color you want. If they stay blue, or turn dark orange with black tips, have a qualified service technician adjust the burner.

A gas smell is different. If you smell gas, leave and follow "Safety & gas smell."

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass once a year. Only do it when the fireplace is completely cool.

  1. Clear a flat, stable spot big enough to lay the glass assembly down.
  2. Lift the safety screen off its magnets.
  3. Lift out the hearth plate, then lift the component access doors up and out.
  4. With a 7/16" nut driver, remove the (3) nuts at the bottom of the glass valance. Lift the glass frame up and off the (3) tabs at the top of the firebox.
  5. Clean the glass with a fireplace glass cleaner and a soft cloth. Don't use abrasive cleaners, and take care not to scratch it.
  6. Put the glass, hearth plate, doors and safety screen back before you use the fireplace.
Damaged glass? Don't run the fireplace with the glass removed, cracked or broken, and don't strike or slam it. Replacement glass comes only from Hussong Mfg., as a complete assembly (#700-174T), fitted by a qualified service person.

modes.title: Pilot modes: IPI or CPI
modes.html:
Your fireplace's pilot can work two ways. You choose on the remote.

IPI (intermittent)the igniter sparks the pilot each time you turn the fireplace on
CPI (continuous)the pilot stays lit; a snowflake icon shows on the remote

A pilot that stays lit keeps the firebox warm and starts a draft in the vent, so the burner lights with less air-flow disruption.

To switch

  1. With the fireplace off, press Mode until the CPI icon is selected.
  2. Press the up arrow for CPI, or the down arrow to go back to IPI. A single beep confirms.
7-day timeout: in CPI, if the burner hasn't lit for 7 days in a row, the pilot turns itself off. Each time the burner lights, the 7-day timer starts over.

Within 24 hours of continuous pilot flame, the system turns itself off for about 5 seconds to check its safety functions, then repeats your last command. If the pilot stays on when you don't want it, the system is set to CPI. Switch it to IPI.

power.title: Power outages & batteries
power.html:
The fireplace runs on house power, with a backup battery pack so the burner still works in a power outage.

Backup battery holder (control module)(4) AA, not included
Remote(3) AAA, included
  • On backup batteries, only the burner works. The fan won't run.
  • How long backup batteries last depends on their quality and how often the fireplace lights.
  • When the backup batteries are low, the control module double-beeps when you press ON/OFF, and the red LED blinks once at intervals. It accepts no commands until you replace them, then beeps once when powered.
  • When the remote's batteries are low, a battery icon appears on its screen.
The power supply to the fireplace must stay on at all times. It shouldn't have a switch in it.

trouble.title: Won't light? Blinking light?
trouble.html:
When you press ON, the fireplace tries twice to light the pilot. Each try sparks for about 60 seconds, with about 35 seconds between tries. If the pilot still hasn't lit, it locks out and the red LED blinks 3 times, over and over, until you reset it.

Reset after a lockout

  • Press ON/OFF on the remote, wait about 2 seconds, and press it again.
  • Or turn the ON/OFF rocker switch off, wait about 2 seconds, and turn it back on.

Red LED blinks

1 blinkbackup batteries low: replace them
2 blinkspilot flame error: contact your dealer
3 blinkslockout: reset as above

Simple causes to check

  • Is the gas on? There may be more than one shut-off valve between the fireplace and the main gas line.
  • On propane, is there propane in the tank?
  • Is the rocker switch on, and are the remote and backup batteries fresh?
  • Burner won't come on? Make sure the remote is on and its thermostat function is off.
The manual says troubleshooting must be done by a qualified technician. Call one if these checks don't solve it.

safety.title: Safety & gas smell
safety.html:
If you smell gas

  • Don't try to light any appliance.
  • Don't touch any electrical switch, and don't use any phone in your building.
  • Leave the building right away.
  • Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone and follow their instructions. If you can't reach them, call the fire department.

Before each use, smell around the fireplace for gas, right down by the floor. Some gas is heavier than air and settles low.

Around the fireplace

  • Hot glass will cause burns. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the safety screen in place. It protects children and other at-risk people from the hot glass. If it's damaged, replace it with Hussong Mfg.'s barrier for this fireplace.
  • Watch young children closely in the same room. A safety gate can keep at-risk people out of the room.
  • Keep clothing and anything flammable off and away from the fireplace. Never store or use gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids nearby.
  • Never burn wood, coal, paper or cardboard in it.
  • If any part has been under water, don't use the fireplace. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.

service.title: Annual service
service.html:
Have a professional service person inspect the fireplace before use and at least once a year. It may need cleaning more often if there's a lot of lint from carpeting or bedding.

Glass cleaningyou, once a year
Firebox, vent system, burner and pilotservice person, once a year
Fanservice person, every 6 months

What the service visit covers

  • Vacuuming the firebox, the fan and the burner system. The fan bearings are sealed and need no oil.
  • Checking gas tubes and connections for leaks.
  • Checking the vent system and that nothing blocks the air flow.
  • Checking that the burner lights within 4 seconds and the flames are steady, not lifting or floating.
  • Inspecting the glass for cracks, scratches and nicks.
Keep the area around the fireplace clear of anything that can burn, and of gasoline and other flammable vapors and liquids.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg.'s limited lifetime warranty covers the original purchaser, from the date of purchase, against defects in materials and workmanship.

30 days · parts and laborpaint, light bulbs, gasket material, glass media and media dam
Year 1 · parts and laborall other parts and material, subject to the exclusions
Years 2 through lifetime · parts onlyfirebox, heat exchanger, logs, burner tube or pan, outer shell, heat shield(s), front viewing glass (thermal shock only), refractory firebox liner (not enamel or glass panels)

Labor is reimbursed to an authorized dealer only. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model. If you notice a defect, contact your authorized dealer within 30 days.

What voids or limits it

  • Not installed by a licensed, authorized technician or contractor, or not installed, operated and maintained per the manual.
  • Serial number or testing label removed, or the fireplace altered.
  • Water damage, or long periods of dampness.
  • It doesn't transfer to a new owner, and doesn't cover normal wear, venting problems or how well it heats your space.

specInlet.html:
Natural gas min / max5" WC (1.25 kPa) / 10.5" WC (2.62 kPa)
Natural gas recommended7" WC (1.74 kPa)
Propane min / max12" WC (2.99 kPa) / 13" WC (3.24 kPa)

Measure at the valve's IN tap (A) with a manometer on a ¼ in (6mm) I.D. hose, with all other gas appliances in the house on or at full capacity. Loosen the tap, attach the manometer, light pilot and burner and confirm the reading is between minimum and maximum. Turn off burner and pilot, disconnect the hose and retighten the tap snug without over-tightening. Relight pilot and burner, reattach the manometer and confirm it reads no pressure. If the reading is too high or too low, contact the gas company; only a qualified gas service technician should adjust incoming pressure.

Disconnect the appliance and its shut-off valve from the supply piping for any pressure test above ½ psi (3.5 kPa); at or below ½ psi, isolate it by closing its manual shut-off valve.

conflicts.issue: Minimum vertical rise for combination venting is printed as 18" (610mm) on p. 34 (natural gas) and p. 36 (propane), while p. 35 renders 18" as 457mm; the inch and metric values disagree.

Venturi direction for blue, lifting flames: p. 52 says opening the air shutter causes a short, blue flame that may lift off the burner, and its Table 11.4 says to close the setting slightly for short, blue flames (venturi open too far) but to open the venturi slightly for lifting (ghosting) flames (venturi closed too far; its other listed cause is gas pressure too high); the troubleshooting chart on p. 55 says to open the air shutter slightly when the flame burns blue and lifts off the burner (and cites Section 11.2.2 Vent Restriction).

p. 30 prints the approved Kozy Heat #800 Series Flexible Direct Vent System as 5" (127mm) x 8" (177mm); the same page gives the appliance's co-axial vent as 5" (127mm) exhaust by 8" (203mm) air intake, and pp. 14 and 21 also give 8" as 203mm (p. 38 gives the #800-1 kit's pipes as 5" & 8"). The guide keeps 8" (203mm) and adds a small note on the 177mm figure.

catalog_mismatches.manual: "Optional fan component will not function on battery back up power" (p. 43; the fan is also marked [optional] on the wiring schematic). The parts list (p. 58) shows the fan kit, Fan Assembly - (2) 75 CFM AL36-028, without saying standard or optional.

review.notes: Not checkable against the manual: it publishes no efficiency (catalog 69.77% NG / 71.34% LP AFUE), no weight (catalog 315 lb) and no 23-3/8" depth (catalog depth_in 23.375). Catalog height 41-11/16", width 46-1/2" and view area 38-1/4 x 32-1/16 appear only as unlabeled values in the dimension drawing (Figure 2.1, p. 9), which the guide does not transcribe. Shown as diagrams and not transcribed: appliance dimensions (p. 9), safety barrier dimensions (p. 10), corner installation (p. 14), vent termination framing (p. 17), outdoor overhang drawings (pp. 18-19; only the text rule is referenced), mantel and facing zones (pp. 22-25), combination venting charts Figures 7.3/7.4 (pp. 35, 37), termination location drawing (p. 29) and log placement figures (p. 42). p. 11 prints the propane kit across a line break as "#LCK-AL36-" / "L-S"; the parts list (p. 58) gives LCK-AL36L-S, which the guide uses. Table 5.1 (p. 27): the word "recommended" also appears in the propane row, but the extracted text does not show which value it applies to, so the guide gives a recommended pressure for natural gas only (7" WC). p. 30 gives the #800 Series as 5" (127mm) x 8" (177mm) while the same page gives 8" as 203mm (inch values agree; metric typo). Section 10.9.5 'Turn OFF the appliance' (p. 49) repeats the turn-on wording ('With the system in the OFF position... to turn ON the appliance'); the guide just says press ON/OFF to turn it off, as the section's result describes. The accent light is called 'if applicable' (p. 50) though the halogen bulbs ship in the components packet (p. 44). Warranty page is dated July 2018 inside the August 2020 (R.8) manual. Termination clearance rows in the 'Vent system & termination' step drawer are taken from the Canadian/US text table on p. 29; the Massachusetts 10' (3m) note is read as part of the US column for row K. Pages 2, 4, 6 and 60 have no extractable text (QA warning; likely blank pages).
